rationale: A pluggable exporter class implementing the Exporter interface. It converts the model to GraphML for external visualization tools and is used by the export command and the MCP export manager. It is a notable replaceable component in the export subsystem. It starts its own telemetry spans, so observability is true. It returns a string and writes no files itself.

Small lookup helper that wraps the relationship catalog query and extracts cardinality and strength for a triple. It serves the relationship command, but it is a thin accessor below the granularity of an architectural element, so it is not modelled as an element.

Private string-sanitizing helper that replaces path traversal and illegal characters before file names are built. It is a trivial implementation detail of AIEvaluator and does no I/O itself, so it is not an architectural element.

Passive TypeScript interface carrying changeset diff results (additions, modifications, deletions) between virtual projection and preview/diff display code. It is an in-code data carrier, not persisted or published as a schema, so it is an application DataObject. It is a notable structure in the changeset preview flow but not a core boundary.

Concrete chat client adapter wrapping the external GitHub Copilot CLI via subprocess. It is a replaceable component implementing BaseChatClient and serves as an integration point. It emits telemetry spans and applies default permission flags when launching the CLI, which counts as authorization handling.

A bundled JSON Schema document that defines the spec's testing-layer node types, such as coveragetarget and testcasesketch. It is a published data contract consumed by tooling, so it belongs in the data model. It is not a test asset. It is architecturally significant as one of the 13 layer schema definitions.

Nested recursive helper inside computeDirectoryHashes that walks a directory and hashes files. It is a private implementation detail, not an architectural element. It reads files from disk, so data_persistence applies; console.error logging is incidental, not telemetry.

A readonly TypeScript interface whose only job is to carry backup state (a file list and a timestamp). It is passive data with no behaviour and is not published as a schema, so it fits a DataObject. It has no callers and only matters to the backup module, so significance is minor. It does no persistence I/O itself.

Static configuration module declaring per-layer expected relationship patterns used by the audit gap analysis. It is passive reference data (an interface plus a constant table) with no behaviour or callers recorded. It is best modelled as an application data object of minor significance within the audit analysis component.

An internal helper of CbmAnalyzer that normalises a raw CBM graph node into a route record with default values. It is called only by verify() and exposed solely for testability. This is data-shaping logic below the level an architecture model would name as an element.

GapAnalyzer is a class in the relationship-audit subsystem. The AuditOrchestrator constructs it, and it compares layer relationship templates against the catalog to propose missing-relationship candidates. It is a cohesive internal unit that a maintainer would name when explaining the audit module, but it is not a system boundary, so it is significant at level 2.

A small exported TypeScript interface that carries validation summary state (validity flag, last-validated timestamp, error and warning counts) inside the stats collector. It is a passive in-code data structure, neither persisted nor published as a schema, so it is an application data object of minor significance.

An in-memory BFS traversal method on the GraphModel class. It is a minor internal operation of the graph component and is delegated to by Model.traverse. As application behaviour it is a function, but its granularity is low. It performs no I/O, security or UI work.

A trivial colour-formatting getter that wraps ansis bold green styling behind a colour-support check. It is a formatting utility, not an architectural element. Its CLI output role is incidental and too small to count as implementing the user-interface concern.

A utility module of file-hashing helpers used for change detection of integration files. It reads files from disk, but it is a low-level helper below the granularity a maintainer would name as an architectural element, so it is not modelled as a node on its own.

Core component that loads the bundled predicate catalog and relationship schemas from disk and exposes relationship type definitions. It is used by the audit orchestrators, the CLI catalog and relationship commands, and report generation. As a central structural unit it is an application component; it reads schema files from disk, so data persistence applies.

A small fallback helper that reads the version from package.json in dev mode, called only by getCliVersion. It is an implementation detail below the level an architecture model would record. Reading package.json at load time and logging to the console on failure are incidental, not persistence or observability concerns.

A small internal TypeScript interface describing the shape of the compiled spec bundle (version, schemas, predicates) that the spec loader reads. It is a passive in-code data structure with no behaviour, so it is a minor application data object rather than a published schema.

This SpecDataService method derives the valid relationship predicates between two node types from the spec loader. It is a query operation of the service that supports relationship validation and suggestion. It is notable but small, has no callers and does no I/O itself, so it is classed as an application function.

A plain options interface that carries CLI export command parameters (format, output path, layers, model, includeSources). It is a passive data carrier of minor significance, used only within its command file, so it is modelled as an application data object.

A trivial text-formatting helper that wraps a string in ANSI dim styling when colour output is enabled. It is a formatting utility below the granularity of an architecture element and has no callers recorded. It only styles terminal output and does not itself drive a user interface.

Registers the MCP resource surface (spec manifest, base, layer schemas, model manifest, annotations) onto an MCP server. It is the access point through which external MCP clients reach model data over the MCP protocol, so it is an application interface. It reads bundled schemas, the model and the annotation store from disk.

Utility module providing kebab-case conversion, element ID formatting, and UUID generation. It is a set of small pure string-formatting helpers below the granularity of an architectural element. Although it encodes the ID convention, it remains a trivial helper and has no callers recorded.

Class coordinating the model relationship audit: loads the project model and relationship catalog, partitions relationships by layer, and runs the coverage, gap, duplicate and balance analyzers to produce an AuditReport. It is a cohesive component invoked by the audit command. Persistence is flagged because it reads the model from disk via Model.load.

A private method of ClaudeCodeAgent that monitors the spawned Claude Code subprocess, collects its stdout and stderr, parses the output into events and resolves the result. It is an internal behaviour of the agent component that handles external subprocess integration, but it sits below the level a maintainer would name as a model element.

This module defines the abstract contract (BaseChatClient plus message, session and option types) that all AI chat CLI integrations (Claude Code, Copilot) implement. It is a central integration abstraction, so it is modelled as an application interface. It is abstract and performs no external calls itself, so no concerns apply.

An exported TypeScript interface that only carries relationship-type metadata (predicate, inverse, category) for the relationship registry. It has no behaviour and its shape is not published as a schema, so it is an application data object. It is a minor internal type with no callers.

Internal step of the upgrade command that installs the spec reference. It is a unit of behaviour inside the upgrade command component, so it is an application function. It creates its own telemetry span and prints CLI output. Persistence is delegated to installSpecReference, so data_persistence is false.

A formatting method that builds a colored CLI error message string from the error's context and suggestions. It is a presentation helper below architectural granularity. It does format CLI output, so the user_interface concern applies, but it is not a modelled element.

Module housing the SemanticValidator class, a named validation component in the validator pipeline. It checks relationship predicates against the spec index and APM provenance rules. This is ordinary application logic, a notable internal unit a maintainer would name when explaining validation. It does no I/O, telemetry or UI rendering itself.

A small internal interface that carries statistics used only for formatting validation output inside one file. It has no callers outside the file and no behaviour of its own, so it sits below the granularity of an architectural element.

Express middleware that authenticates MCP HTTP requests by extracting a Bearer token and validating it via ApiKeyManager, rejecting with 401. It is the identity-verification mechanism protecting the MCP HTTP transport boundary, so it is best modelled as the security layer's authentication configuration and is architecturally significant.

An injected analysis class in the relationship audit subsystem. It computes per-layer coverage metrics (isolation, predicate utilization, density) from the relationship catalog and is used by AuditOrchestrator. That makes it a notable internal component, not an entry point. Its console warnings are incidental error reporting, not telemetry or a user interface.

Core behaviour of the JSON Schema exporter: transforms data-model graph nodes and edges into a Draft-7 schema string. It is internal export logic performed by the exporter component, so it is an application function. It creates telemetry spans and attributes itself, and returns a string rather than writing to files.

A small options interface carrying three flags for the staging area's commit operation. It is a passive in-code data structure with no behaviour, so it is a minor application data object. It is an implementation-level parameter bag of low architectural significance.

Pluggable exporter class implementing the Exporter interface that converts the data-model layer of a model into a JSON Schema Draft 7 document. It is invoked by the CLI export command and the MCP export tool. It is a notable component in the export subsystem, and it starts its own telemetry spans directly. It does not write any files.

Small exported helper that checks the filesystem for existing .md layer reports; used only by the upgrade command. It reads a directory on disk but is an implementation detail rather than a named architectural element.

Trivial delegating accessor on SpecDataService that forwards a lookup to SpecDataLoader. It is used widely, but it is a one-line wrapper below the granularity of an architecture element. The owning service would be the modelled component, not this method.

The module persists chat session transcripts (messages, commands, errors) to per-session files under .dr/chat/sessions. This is a user-facing history store rather than OpenTelemetry telemetry, so it fits best as an application component. It writes files on disk, so data_persistence applies. It is a notable utility module but not core.

Exported class that binds all model tools onto the MCP server, acting as the integration point exposing tools to external MCP clients. It wraps each handler in a telemetry span and sets the error status. This is a structural component wiring the MCP surface, so it is classified as an applicationcomponent.

A plain options interface carrying CLI flags for the visualize command. It is a passive data structure with no behaviour, so it is an application DataObject of minor significance. Its auth-related fields (noAuth, token) are only configuration values; the interface performs no authentication itself.

A private formatting helper that appends a markdown table section of matched entries to a lines buffer. It is called only by formatVerifyMarkdown. As a pure formatting utility it sits below architectural granularity and does no I/O or rendering of its own.

A thin orchestrator step that delegates to DuplicateDetector, optionally scoped to one layer. It is one internal stage of the audit orchestration, called only by runAudit, so it is a minor application function. Its log call merely delegates and does not itself implement observability.

MCP tool module exposing a 'model_stats' operation to external MCP clients; it is a consumer-facing unit of application behaviour that wraps StatsCollector. It defines the tool contract and handler served over MCP (external integration). It is one of many similar tools, so it is notable rather than core.

A report-generation class that renders the model README markdown from ModelReadmeData. It is instantiated by ModelReportOrchestrator and is a named internal unit of the reporting module. It returns a string and does no file I/O itself. Its output is generated documentation, not a user interface.

Validates source-predicate-destination triples against the relationship catalog and generates suggestions; this is the CLI's catalog-enforcement behaviour described in the charter. It is an internal function used by the add-relationship command handler, so it is a notable application function rather than a service or a trivial helper.

A bundled JSON Schema document that defines the security layer's node types and their attribute schemas for the specification. It is a central data-model contract the CLI validates models against. It describes security concepts but does not itself authenticate or authorize anything, so no cross-cutting concerns apply.

An in-memory graph mutation method on the GraphModel component. It removes a node, updates the layer and type indices, and cascades edge removal. This is internal behaviour of the model component rather than a named service, so it is a minor application function. No storage I/O is involved.

A passive in-code data structure holding a projected (virtual) model state: manifest, layers and relationships, plus an isProjection marker that guards against accidental saves. It carries data between parts of the program and is not a published schema, so it is an application data object. It is notable within the virtual-projection module.

A class used by AuditOrchestrator that analyses the relationship catalog for semantically overlapping predicates, with cached results. It is a cohesive analysis unit inside the audit subsystem, so it is modelled as an application component. It is a notable internal part rather than a boundary. Its console warnings are incidental debugging, not telemetry.

An exported TypeScript interface that only carries per-category relationship classification statistics (count, percentage, predicates, strength) within the analysis module. It is a passive in-code data structure, not persisted or published as a schema, so it is an application data object of minor significance.

Small exported helper that writes MCP tool failures to stderr. It does logging work, so observability applies. However, it is an implementation detail called only by runTool, not a modelled log record or log configuration, and falls below the granularity of an architecture element.

Bundled JSON Schema document defining the application layer's node schemas (ApplicationComponent, ApplicationService, and others) with $schema and $id URNs. It is a core schema contract that the tool validates models against, so it fits data-model JSONSchema. As a static definition file it performs no behaviour and implements none of the cross-cutting concerns.

Private helper that assembles the final VerifyReport object from precomputed buckets and summary counts. It is pure data shaping with no I/O. It is an implementation detail of VerifyEngine.computeReport, not a separately modelled architectural element.

Module holding PromptTemplates, which builds the LLM prompts used by the AI relationship-audit feature. This is internal application behaviour that supports the audit pipeline. It is a notable unit a maintainer would name, but it is not a boundary or a service in its own right. It only formats strings and does not call external systems itself.

A plain TypeScript interface that carries per-layer audit summary metrics (counts and quality scores) between parts of the audit module. It is an in-code data carrier with no behaviour, so it is an application data object. It is a minor internal unit with no callers.

Shared CLI error type used by 63 callers. It carries an exit code, suggestions and context, and formats coloured CLI output. It is a passive carrier of error state with a formatting method, so it fits best as an application data object. It is a notable cross-cutting convention but not a service.

A static method that computes model validation statistics: element counts per layer, relationship counts by predicate, and orphan detection. It is internal behaviour of the validation formatter, reused by CLI commands and the MCP handler. A maintainer would name it, but it is not a service boundary. It operates on in-memory model data only, so no cross-cutting concern applies.

Trivial accessor returning a build-time constant or falling back to a dev version resolver. Widely used, but it is a utility helper below architectural granularity; it implements no cross-cutting concern itself.

Exported validator class that the composite Validator composes. It encapsulates semantic rule checks: relationship predicates against the spec index, and an APM provenance warning. It is a cohesive, replaceable application unit within the validation pipeline, notable but not central. It performs no I/O, telemetry or UI work itself.

The module implements the RelationshipValidator, a cohesive validation component in the CLI. It loads the bundled relationship schemas from manifest files on disk and enforces predicate, type and cardinality rules on model relationships. It also wraps its work in telemetry spans. This is a significant validation component, not an API, data schema or test asset.

A small internal type pairing an MCP server instance with its HTTP transport for session bookkeeping inside the HTTP transport module. It is an implementation detail, not a domain data object or a contract, so it is not modelled as an architecture element.

Orchestrates the CLI upgrade workflow as ordered steps: display plan, handle dry-run, confirm with user, then execute spec, model and integration upgrades in sequence. It renders CLI output and prompts, and sets span attributes and records exceptions. It is an internal process behind the upgrade command, not the entry point itself.

Module containing ExportManager, the registry and dispatcher for format-specific exporters. It is a cohesive, replaceable component central to the export subsystem: it registers exporters, validates layer support and delegates export. It does no I/O itself.

Private helper that shallow-copies a Layer and its elements for the projection engine. It is an in-memory cloning implementation detail with no I/O and no exposed behaviour, so it sits below the granularity of an architecture element.

An abstract base class that defines the common contract for AI chat CLI integrations (availability, sendMessage, sessions). It is a central abstraction that concrete clients specialize, so it is modelled as an application component. The base class itself only holds in-memory session state; subclasses perform the subprocess integration, so external_integration is false here.

CLI subcommand handler ('dr schema types <layer>') that validates the layer ID, queries the spec data service for node types and prints them to the console. It is a user-invocable entry point but a narrow listing command, so it is modelled as an application function with CLI output as its user interface concern.

Method of MutationHandler that performs element deletion, either staging it in the active changeset or removing it and its relationships from the base model and persisting. It is a cohesive internal behaviour shared by the CLI and MCP delete paths, so it is an application function of notable but not top-level significance.

The module registers the full DR model tool surface onto an MCP server. That makes it the MCP access point through which the application's services are reached, so it is an ApplicationInterface. It serves an external protocol, an integration boundary. It also wraps each tool handler in tracing spans and sets error status, so observability is true.

A tiny TypeScript interface describing the parsed shape of a manifest file within a validator module. It is a local typing helper with no callers or behaviour, so it sits below the granularity of an architecture element.

An exported analysis class that wraps the relationship catalog and classifies model relationships by category, layer crossing and semantics. It also computes category breakdowns and transitivity analysis. It is a cohesive analysis unit with an injected dependency, so it is an application component. Its only caller is a test, so it is notable internally but not central.

A CLI subcommand handler helper that validates a snapshot exists and deletes it via SnapshotStorage, printing confirmation. It is a small internal unit of the audit-snapshots command; persistence is delegated to SnapshotStorage, and it renders CLI output directly.

Utility module holding global CLI option state with trivial getters/setters and conditional console logging helpers. It is scaffolding/configuration plumbing below the granularity a maintainer would name as an architectural element; the logging is incidental console output, not telemetry.

ExportManager is the central registry and dispatcher for format-specific exporters, used by both the CLI export command and the MCP export tool. It is a cohesive, replaceable structural unit that owns the export capability, so it is an application component. It performs no I/O itself.

Trivial state mutator that resets an in-memory array on the FarmSyncState class. It has no callers, performs no I/O and holds no logic, so it is an implementation detail below architectural granularity rather than a model element.

A small exported TypeScript interface that carries error metadata (operation, context, related elements, partial progress) inside an error utility module. It is a passive in-code data carrier, so it fits the application data object type. It has no callers and is a minor internal utility type, hence low significance.

Internal core function in the attribute-collision repair module that searches changeset history to recover lost attribute values. It is a notable unit of repair behaviour invoked by the repair command. Persistence is delegated to StagedChangesetStorage.list, so the function itself does no storage work.

An in-memory computation of graph statistics (node, edge and cycle counts, and connected components) on the DependencyTracker. It has no callers and is a minor analytic method of the component, not telemetry in the APM sense. It is at most a small internal application function.

Exported TypeScript interface that carries drift-detection results (hashes, drift flag, affected layers and elements) between parts of the snapshot manager. It is a passive in-code data structure, neither persisted nor published as a schema, so it is an application DataObject of moderate significance.

ImportManager is a registry and dispatcher that selects among the registered format importers (ArchiMate, OpenAPI) and delegates model import to them. It is a cohesive, replaceable module behind the import command, so it is modelled as an application component and is architecturally significant as the import subsystem's facade.

A trivial helper method that reads and trims the spec/VERSION file for the audit loader. It is an implementation detail of NodeSchemaLoader, below the granularity of an architecture element. It does read a file from disk, so the data persistence concern applies.

A small path-resolution helper that joins the model subdirectory onto the project root and checks that it exists. It is a utility used by several commands, below the granularity a maintainer would name as an architectural element. It only checks file existence and performs no durable reads or writes.

The module defines SpecDataService, a high-level service class that wraps SpecDataLoader. It offers query, analysis and caching over specification metadata. As a cohesive, replaceable unit central to spec operations, it is an application component. File I/O happens in the loader, not here, so data_persistence is false; the in-memory cache is not durable storage.

CLI command module implementing `dr docs generate/validate`. It is a cohesive unit of command behaviour that spawns a bun subprocess, reads and writes files on disk, and prints CLI output. Maintainers would name it as the docs command module, which is a notable but not core component.

GraphModel is the central in-memory graph abstraction holding nodes, edges and query indices. Model, Layer and RelationshipGraph all build on it, making it a core application component of the Documentation Robotics tool. It is purely in-memory: it performs no persistence, I/O or UI work.

An options interface that only carries parameters (agent, working directory, session id, danger flag, output stream) into chat client calls. It is an in-code data carrier, not a published schema, so it is an application data object. It is minor and only matters to the chat client module.

A plain input DTO carrying the fields used to create an annotation in the annotation store. It is not persisted itself and is not published as a schema, so it is an application data object of minor significance. It implements no cross-cutting concern on its own.

Private helper that counts balance assessments by category and status for markdown report generation. It is a trivial aggregation utility below the granularity a maintainer would name in an architecture model, so it is not an element.

Exported function that reads and validates the analyzer session state from .dr/analyzers/session.json. It is an internal persistence routine used by the analyzer commands: a notable unit within the session-state module rather than a service boundary. It reads durable file storage directly.

A small shared module of zod field validators reused by the annotation MCP tool input schemas. These are reusable field-level fragments, not a contract or entity of their own, so the module sits below modelling granularity. The MCP tool definitions that use them are what would be modelled.

Private helper that serializes an AI layer review to a JSON file in the output directory. It writes durable storage, but it is an implementation detail of AIEvaluator rather than a named architectural element.

A tiny exported type holding two optional matching fields (handler, path) for a verify-ignore rule. It is an implementation-level data shape inside the analyzer, with no callers, no behaviour and no architectural standing of its own. It sits below the granularity a maintainer would name.

CLI command handler for 'changeset revert': loads the model, delegates the revert to StagingAreaManager, and renders CLI/JSON output. It also creates and annotates telemetry spans itself. Persistence is delegated to the manager. It is a notable unit of CLI behaviour, best modelled as an application function, not a core service.

A storage manager class that owns the persistence of staged changesets as YAML files on disk. It is a repository-like component used widely by commands, the model, the staging area and the server, which makes it a significant application component with a file-persistence concern rather than a database store layer element.

A pluggable exporter class implementing the Exporter interface. It transforms the model's API layer into an OpenAPI 3.0 document. It is a replaceable component used by both the CLI export command and the MCP export tool. It starts telemetry spans directly. It does not itself write files or call external systems.

CLI command module for 'dr reports regenerate'. It registers the subcommand, deletes and recreates the reports directory on disk, and drives the report orchestrator, printing console output. As an ordinary application module it is a notable CLI component, though not central to the architecture.

A one-line, test-only helper that clears an in-memory module-private cache between test cases. It is scaffolding below the granularity of an architecture element and touches no durable storage. It also implements no cross-cutting concern.

An MCP tool module that exposes the 'changeset_show' operation to external agents, wrapping StagingAreaManager. MCP tools are not OpenAPI contracts, so this is best modelled as an application service. It serves an external MCP protocol boundary. Loading is delegated to the staging area, so persistence is not implemented here. It is one of many similar tools.

Simple accessor on RelationshipCatalog that derives category names from loaded relationship types via in-memory iteration. It is a small helper method below architectural granularity; the catalog class itself would be the modelled component. No I/O beyond the delegated ensureLoaded call.

VerifyEngine is a cohesive analyzer class that computes drift/verification reports by matching discovered graph routes against the model's API layer. It is a named component in the verify feature, invoked by CbmAnalyzer. It loads the model and ignore rules from disk, which counts as data persistence work.

A small TypeScript interface describing the shape of the analyzer registry manifest: a spec version plus a list of analyzer metadata entries. It is a passive data structure with no behaviour, used inside the registry module, so it is an application data object of minor significance.

A plain TypeScript interface that carries drift-analysis results: model elements with no counterpart in the code graph. It is an in-code data carrier passed between analyzer parts, so it is an application data object. As one minor entry type in the analyzer types file, it has low significance.
Trivial accessor returning a field from a global options object. It has no behaviour beyond the read and sits below the granularity of an architecture element, as a private helper or accessor.

A small query method on DependencyTracker that wraps graph descent to list transitive dependencies. It has no callers and is a thin accessor below the component granularity, so it is not an architectural element in its own right. The parent DependencyTracker class would be the element modelled.

Core module housing DependencyTracker, which performs graph-based dependency tracing and impact analysis over model elements via the reference registry. It is a cohesive internal analysis component a maintainer would name, but not an entry point or boundary. It performs no I/O, rendering, or auth work.

A custom OTLP SpanExporter that sends spans as JSON over HTTP POST (fetch) to a configured collector endpoint with a timeout. It is a telemetry export destination and transport binding, so it maps to apm exporterconfig. It integrates externally with the collector and is a notable telemetry integration point.

Exported TypeScript interface defining the shape of the repository context (Git URL and commit SHA) within a source reference. It is part of the spec's published source_reference schema, so it is an object schema. Being a small nested value type with no callers, its significance is minor.

A small wrapper inside the upgrade command. It runs a supplied update callback, prints CLI progress and error lines, and records an 'upgrade.integration' span. This is a private-level helper below modelling granularity. It implements tracing and console output itself, but it is not a standalone architectural element.

An in-memory mutation method on GraphModel that removes an edge and maintains its source, destination and predicate indices. It is an implementation detail of the graph model component, not an element a maintainer would name on its own. No durable storage or other cross-cutting concern is involved.

Module defines the read-safe tool permission allowlist for AI coding agents (Claude Code, Copilot), validates it, and formats it for CLI flags. It is an authorization policy deciding what agents may do, and is shared by both integrations, which makes it architecturally significant. It touches external CLIs via spawnSync and format adapters.

A small internal TypeScript type describing the OpenAPI tag shape that the exporter emits. It is a typing helper for export serialization, not an API tag of the system itself, and it is below architectural granularity: trivial boilerplate with no callers or behaviour.

A shared, exported runner class used by audit evaluators to invoke Claude. It wraps the external AI call with rate limiting, timeout and fail-fast logic. This makes it a reusable application component and the integration point to an external AI system.

Trivial state accessor on GoldenCopyCacheManager returning whether in-memory fields are set. It has no callers and does no I/O, so it is an implementation detail rather than a modelled element. The owning cache manager class would be the application component.

Trivial test-support helper that clears a module-level singleton reference. It has no behaviour beyond assigning undefined and exists only so tests can reset state. It is scaffolding, not an architectural element, and it emits no telemetry itself.

Module housing the GraphMLExporter, a pluggable implementation of the Exporter interface that serialises the model to GraphML for external graph tools. It is a notable, replaceable export component within the export subsystem. It emits a telemetry span itself. It returns a string rather than writing to disk, so persistence is not set.

FarmManifest is a core domain class that loads, validates, mutates and saves farm.yaml to disk. Because it encapsulates both state and persistence behaviour (file I/O, YAML parsing, validation), it is an application component rather than a passive data object. It is central to multi-project farm management.

A passive result type carrying the outcome of applying model-version migrations between parts of the program. It has no behaviour and is not a persisted entity or published schema, so it is an application DataObject of minor significance, relevant mainly to the migration registry.

Exported CLI entry-point command that launches the interactive AI chat session. It detects and selects external chat CLIs (Claude Code, Copilot) and starts a spawned client, renders CLI prompts and output, and opens telemetry spans and log records itself. It is a user-facing application service in the CLI, so it is architecturally significant.

This WebSocket JSON-RPC 2.0 dispatcher is the access point for chat functionality. It routes chat.status, chat.send and chat.cancel requests and kills chat subprocesses, which counts as external integration. Because it is a protocol channel binding rather than an HTTP OpenAPI operation, it fits best as an application interface on the VisualizationServer component.

An MCP tool module that exposes the model_delete operation to external agents. It loads the model, traces dependents, and deletes elements, with cascade or force options, through MutationHandler. It is a consumer-facing operation of the MCP server, so it is an application service. It persists model changes and serves an external MCP client.

A trivial error subclass that only presets the message, category and CLI suggestions for a missing element. It is boilerplate error-handling detail below the granularity of an architecture element and has no callers recorded. It builds hint text but does not itself render the CLI.

Exported TypeScript interface defining the shape of the source_reference attribute on model elements (provenance, locations, repository). This is a domain data type whose shape is published as part of the spec schema, so it is modelled as an object schema. It is a notable but not central structure.

A small helper that maps the generated spec registry into a per-layer list of element-type ids for the conformance command. It is a data-reshaping utility below the granularity a maintainer would name as an architectural element, and it performs no I/O or other cross-cutting work.

A trivial one-line lookup method on RelationshipRegistry that checks map membership. It has no callers and is an accessor-level helper below the granularity at which the model records elements; the registry class itself would be the modelled component.

A result type for the golden copy cache's clone operation. It carries the cloned model, its root path, a cleanup callback and timing stats, and has no behaviour of its own. That makes it a minor application data object. It is not persisted or published as a schema, so it is not a data-model object schema.

Core engine class that computes merged model projections from staged changesets, with an in-memory TTL cache. It is used by the staging area manager, the changeset validator and the model, so it is a significant application component. It loads changesets from on-disk staged storage, which counts as durable reads.

A small pure helper that grades confidence by comparing predicate categories and semantics. Its only caller is detectModelDuplicates in the same file. This is an implementation detail of the duplicate-detection audit, not a standalone architectural element, and it touches no cross-cutting concern.

A small utility module of call-graph helpers: depth clamping, node shaping and edge-type selection. These are pure transformation helpers with no callers recorded. The module sits below the granularity a maintainer would name as an architectural element. Its console.warn is incidental and does not amount to observability work.

A one-line delegating method on SpecDataService that forwards a filter query to SpecDataLoader. It is a trivial wrapper with no callers and no logic of its own. The owning service class would be the modelled element, not this method.

A small in-memory implementation of the ProgressTracker interface. It tracks completed evaluation keys for the AI evaluator. It is a minor internal helper used only by AIEvaluator, with no persistence, I/O or telemetry, so it has low significance within the application layer.

Module housing the ReportGenerator class, which renders audit results as JSON, markdown or text and writes them to disk. It is a cohesive internal component of the audit subsystem, notable but not central, and it persists files. Report formatting is application output rather than telemetry, so the observability concern does not apply.

A no-op stub property on a noop span object that just returns the span itself. It is trivial telemetry scaffolding with no callers and no behaviour, and it falls below the granularity of an architectural element. It does no actual telemetry work, so no concern is flagged.

Private helper incrementing an in-memory cache-hit counter inside VirtualProjectionEngine. It is an implementation detail, not a telemetry instrument or exported metric. It does no durable storage, so no cross-cutting concern applies and it is below modelling granularity.

Passive TypeScript interface that holds categorized verify results (matched, graph-only, model-only, ignored) and is passed between analyzer code. It is an in-code data carrier with no behaviour and no published schema, so it is an application data object of minor significance.

Utility module providing a file-based locking mechanism (lockfiles via atomic mkdir, stale-lock cleanup) that guards read-modify-write of changeset files. It is a notable internal concurrency component rather than a domain service. It writes and removes lock directories on disk, which counts as data persistence.

Central domain entity of the architecture model: the Element class mirrors spec-node.schema.json (id, type, layer_id, attributes, source_reference, relationships) with serialization to and from that schema. Its shape is published as a schema, so it is an object schema. It is used across the commands, the layer, the model and the MCP tools, which makes it a core abstraction.

A tiny internal type pairing an HTTP method with endpoint data inside the OpenAPI exporter. It is a local implementation helper structure, has no callers, and is not a published schema or contract, so it falls below the granularity of an architectural element.

An exported function that reads and validates a per-analyzer status JSON file from disk. It is a small persistence helper within the session-state module and is only called from tests, so it has minor significance as an application function. It implements data persistence through its file reads.

Private filtering helper inside GapAnalyzer that matches node type names against a pattern. It is a trivial implementation detail with a single caller and no I/O, so it is not an architectural element on its own.

A custom Error subclass that signals an abort after repeated AI evaluation failures. It is error-handling boilerplate inside the runner rather than a named architectural element. It does no integration or authentication work itself; it only formats a message.

A trivial CLI options interface with three boolean flags for the upgrade command. It is a parameter bag with no behaviour and no published schema, so it sits below the granularity a maintainer would name. It is an implementation detail of the command, not an architectural element.

A trivial formatting helper that wraps text in ANSI red when colours are enabled. It is an implementation detail with no architectural identity, so it is not modelled as an element. It only formats strings and does not itself render or drive CLI output.

Module of in-code type definitions (CoverageMetrics, DuplicateCandidate, GapCandidate, etc.) carrying audit-system results between parts of the program. These are not persisted or published as schemas, so they are application data objects. The module is notable for explaining the audit subsystem but is not a component itself.

A small CLI options interface with two optional fields (output, layer) for a docs generate command. It is a parameter type local to the command file, so it is an implementation detail rather than a standalone architectural element. It implements no cross-cutting concern.

Types module that defines the Exporter contract every format exporter implements, along with export options, format metadata and shared constants. The Exporter interface is the plug-in access point for the export subsystem. Mostly type declarations and helpers, so it is a notable internal unit rather than a core architectural element.

In-memory collection manager for model relationships, used by Model, with add/delete/query and dirty tracking. It is a cohesive core-domain unit that a maintainer would name. It does no file I/O itself; serialization to YAML happens elsewhere, so data_persistence is false.

Dispatcher method on ChangesetExporter that detects the format and routes to YAML, JSON or patch parsers to import a changeset from a string. It is internal behaviour of the exporter component, a notable unit but not a component itself. It parses in-memory data only, with no file I/O.

An input-validation check rejecting path traversal characters in analyzer names, used only by getStateDir. It is evidence for a security validation rule, but as a small helper its significance is minor. It neither decides access nor touches storage itself.

CLI command module implementing element deletion: loads the model, traces dependents, prompts for confirmation, deletes via the mutation handler (persisting the model) and emits telemetry spans. It is a named unit of CLI behaviour that a maintainer would cite, so it is modelled as an application function of moderate significance.

Private validation helper inside NodeResponseParser that type-checks and clamps fields of one AI evaluation item. It is an implementation detail of the parser, called only by parseLayerEvaluation, and is not an architectural element on its own.

A pure in-memory analyzer class comparing two audit reports (coverage, gaps, duplicates, balance, connectivity) and producing a differential analysis. It is a cohesive, reusable unit used by the pipeline orchestrator and the audit-diff command, so it is a notable application component. It performs no I/O, telemetry or UI work itself.

A plain TypeScript interface carrying the results of a changeset compatibility check between parts of the program. It has no behaviour and is not persisted or published as a schema, so it is an application data object of minor significance.

ApiKeyManager establishes how MCP server clients prove identity. It generates, stores, rotates and validates API keys using a constant-time comparison. It persists key files and config to disk. This makes it the authentication mechanism for the MCP server boundary, best modelled as the security layer's AuthenticationConfig.

Builds the in-memory relationship graph from the spec relationship catalog for audit connectivity analysis. It is internal behaviour of the RelationshipGraph component, invoked by the audit orchestrator, so it is an application function. It is notable within the audit module but is not a service boundary. Its stderr warnings are incidental, not telemetry.

MCP tool handler exposing annotation update to external MCP clients. It validates the arguments and delegates persistence to AnnotationStore, so it is an exposed application service operation at the system boundary. Persistence itself happens in the store; the handler serves an external MCP protocol.

CLI 'add' command module: validates the layer and element type, generates the ID, loads the model, adds the element and saves it. It is a named user-facing CLI operation that drives model mutation. It sets span attributes and prints coloured CLI output. Persistence happens through Model load and save.

Defines the shape of a persisted YAML version file (.dr-version), documented as its schema. A persisted file-format structure maps to a data-model object schema. Notable for integration installation tracking, though it is passive and has no behaviour of its own, so it implements no cross-cutting concern.

Nested output helper inside deleteCommand that formats and prints a CLI success message. It is a trivial presentation detail below the architectural granularity threshold, though it does drive CLI output.

Small internal method of MutationHandler that snapshots an element's JSON into before/after context fields. It is a trivial state-capture helper inside a component, not a nameable architectural element. It does no I/O and implements no cross-cutting concern.

Module providing a shared golden test model cloned via filesystem for test initialization performance. It is test infrastructure (fixture/scaffolding provider), so testing layer; no IEEE-829 coverage element type fits a fixture cache. Writes and copies model directories on disk, so data_persistence is true. It is a notable internal unit, not core architecture.

The class composes a prompt builder, an AI runner and a response parser, and evaluates node schemas per layer with an LLM for the node audit. It is a cohesive application component called by the audit orchestrator. The external Claude call is delegated to AuditAIRunner, so external_integration is false. It writes progress to stderr, which counts as CLI output.

In-code TypeScript interface carrying the parsed contents of a node schema file between audit components. It has no behaviour and is neither persisted nor published as a schema, so it is an application data object. It is a minor internal type with no recorded callers.

Trivial string-formatting helper that splits a camel-cased type name on capitals and title-cases it for display. It is a pure formatting utility used only by another helper in the same file, so it falls below the granularity of an architectural element.

Private formatting helper inside MarkdownGenerator that counts graph nodes and edges and renders a markdown table string. It is an implementation detail of the export component, too fine-grained to be an architectural element, and performs no I/O, auth, telemetry or UI work itself.

A trivial error subclass in a utils module that formats a message and CLI suggestions. It has no callers and is an implementation detail of error handling, below the granularity of an architectural element.

A plain TypeScript interface that holds per-layer relationship counts for report generation. It is an in-code data carrier with no behaviour and no published schema, so it is an application data object. It is a minor unit relevant mainly within the reports module.

The module orchestrates a model audit as an ordered pipeline. It loads the project model from disk, builds per-layer maps, then runs the coverage, gap, duplicate, balance and connectivity analyzers to produce an AuditReport. This is a significant multi-step application process in the audit subsystem. It reads persisted model files, so data_persistence is true.

Exported core function that applies recovered attribute values onto the in-memory model as one step of the attribute-collision repair capability, called by the repair command. It is internal behaviour of the repair module. It does not persist anything itself, because the caller saves the affected layers.

This is the main entry method of StatsCollector. It aggregates layer, relationship, validation, orphan and completeness statistics into a ModelStats result. It is shared by the CLI stats command, report generation and the MCP tool. It is internal application behaviour of the stats component, so it is modelled as an application function. It does no I/O itself.

An exported analyzer class used by NodeAuditOrchestrator to score the quality of node-type definitions: description and attribute documentation. It is a cohesive, replaceable unit of the audit subsystem, so it is modelled as an application component. It is a notable internal unit rather than a system boundary, and it implements no cross-cutting concern itself.

A plain data structure holding cache hit, miss and invalidation counters for the virtual projection engine. It is in-process state, not an OpenTelemetry instrument, so it fits an application data object. It is a minor internal unit of the projection cache that only this file cares about.

A trivial pure helper that clamps a confidence enum from 'high' to 'medium' for service candidates. It is an implementation detail of the analyzer heuristics with no architectural identity of its own, so it is not modelled as an element.

This is the main behaviour of the MarkdownExporter component: it renders a model's manifest, layers and elements into a Markdown document string. It is an internal export function performed by one component. It wraps its work in a telemetry span, so observability is true. It neither writes files nor drives a UI itself.

Registers the CLI 'element' subcommand group (add/list/show/delete/update) on Commander, acting as a CLI access point that delegates to existing command handlers. It is an alternative entry wiring, i.e. an application interface. It defines the CLI surface (user interface) but has no logic of its own, so it is of moderate significance.

Bundled JSON configuration for the codebase-memory-mcp analyzer. It declares the external MCP server's tool contract, binaries and languages, and maps its graph labels to DR layers and element types. It is a versioned, deployed configuration artifact that defines a key external integration point, not executable code or a schema definition.

A pluggable importer class implementing the Importer interface, registered by ImportManager. It parses external OpenAPI specs into model graph nodes and edges. This is a cohesive, replaceable application component and an integration point for an external format. It also emits telemetry spans. It is not itself an API contract.

A plain TypeScript interface that only carries counters and timing statistics for the golden copy cache. It is a passive in-code data structure, so it is an application data object. Significance is minor because it is an internal stats record with no callers. It is not telemetry instrumentation itself.

A no-op span stub method returning noopSpan inside the telemetry module's fallback implementation. It is trivial scaffolding with no behaviour, no callers or callees, and does not itself emit telemetry, so it is not an architectural element.

Private timeout helper that returns a promise rejecting after a delay. It is used only by AuditAIRunner.invoke to race against the AI call. This is a trivial implementation detail with no architectural identity.

Orchestrates an ordered multi-step audit pipeline (before audit, AI evaluation, after audit, differential summary) with a defined end result. It writes reports and snapshots to disk, invokes the Claude CLI via AIEvaluator, and prints progress to the console. This makes it an applicationprocess and an architecturally significant workflow.

Pure analysis module within the audit subsystem that detects semantically overlapping node types in the spec using name and attribute similarity heuristics. It is a notable internal unit of audit behaviour, not a service boundary. It performs no I/O and implements no cross-cutting concern.

A file-local TypeScript interface describing the shape of a parsed layer distribution JSON file, used only within the relationship schema validator. It is an internal typing helper for deserialization, with no callers, and sits below the granularity of an architectural element.

Trivial setter that merges CLI options into a module-level global variable. It is an implementation detail with no behaviour beyond assignment, below the granularity of an architecture element, and implements none of the cross-cutting concerns.

A private helper in StatsCollector that computes the elements with no relationships by walking the in-memory model. It is internal behaviour of one component, called only by collect(). It is a minor unit with no I/O or telemetry of its own, so it is modelled at most as a low-significance application function.

Concrete chat-client adapter that spawns and streams from the external Claude Code CLI subprocess, emitting telemetry spans and writing output to a stream. It is a replaceable integration component behind the BaseChatClient abstraction, so it is architecturally significant as an integration point.

Exported TypeScript interface that only carries the outcome of an import operation (counts and errors) between parts of the program. It is not persisted or published as a schema, so it is an application data object of minor significance.

A bundled JSON Schema document that declares the product layer's metadata and the draft-07 node schemas for capability, feature, milestone, persona and userworkflow. It is a core data contract the tool validates models against, so it is a top-level schema document in the data model. It performs no behaviour itself.

Formatting function that renders a node audit report as a Markdown string. It is a format-specific helper dispatched by formatNodeAuditReport, sits below modelling granularity, and does no I/O itself. It is a formatting utility, not an architectural element.

Trivial statistics accessor on RelationshipRegistry that counts relationships, predicates and layers in memory. It has no callers and is an implementation detail below the granularity of an architecture element. It does no I/O, telemetry, or UI work.

Core module housing the RelationshipRegistry class, an in-memory catalog and index of relationship types and instances by source, layer and predicate. It is a cohesive application component in the model core, with no callers and slated for consolidation into GraphModel, so it is notable but not central. It performs no persistence or I/O.

ReportDataModel is a substantive class with injected collaborators: it aggregates statistics, relationship classification, data-model insights and quality metrics, and caches the results. It forms a cohesive reporting component used by the report command. Despite its name it is not a schema, so it is modelled as an application component. It works only on the in-memory model, so no persistence concern applies.

A trivial readonly type holding a list of node IDs for a connected component in the audit graph analysis. It is a small internal data shape with no callers recorded and no behaviour, which puts it below the granularity of an architecture element.

CLI command handler that explicitly stages a single model element into the active changeset (the docstring says 'remove', but the code adds). It is internal command behaviour inside the changeset command module, invoked by the command registry. It creates telemetry spans directly and writes CLI output. Persistence is delegated to StagingAreaManager, so data_persistence is false.

Public method of NodeOverlapDetector that groups node schemas by layer and compares each pair to find semantic overlap candidates. It is invoked by the audit orchestrator, making it a notable internal analysis behaviour of the audit component. It does no I/O and touches no cross-cutting concern.

A class that composes the coverage, duplicate, gap, balance and connectivity analyzers around the relationship catalog and graph, and orchestrates the relationship audit pipeline. As a cohesive, replaceable unit owning substantive behaviour and its collaborators, it is an application component and a significant element of the audit subsystem. The logging and catalog loading it does are delegated, so no concern applies.

CLI command module implementing element search across the model. It loads the model from disk and renders table/JSON output, making it a notable CLI command unit. It only fetches the active span rather than emitting telemetry itself, so observability is false. It is ordinary application structure, a module-level component owning searchCommand.

A small options interface configuring a file-lock utility's timeouts and stale-lock detection. It is a parameter bag for an internal helper with no callers, not an architectural element, and performs no storage I/O itself.

A trivial state accessor that delegates to the loader's isLoaded() check. It has no callers and no behaviour of its own, so it is an implementation detail of SpecDataService rather than an architectural element.

CLI command handler for 'repair attribute-collision': orchestrates scanning the model for damage, recovering values from changeset history, saving layers and writing reports, and renders CLI output. It is a named, user-invoked command, but a narrow maintenance utility, so it is modelled as an application function of moderate significance.

Shared CLI error-handling module defining error categories with exit codes, a CLIError hierarchy and formatted console output. It is cross-cutting utility infrastructure a maintainer would name when explaining CLI behaviour, but it is not a core service. It renders user-facing CLI error output, so the user_interface concern applies.

Abstract base component for AI-tool integration managers (Claude Code, Copilot) that installs integration files, tracks version files on disk and detects updates. It is a central abstraction for the integrations module and directly reads and writes files and version manifests.

A plain TypeScript interface that carries computed complexity statistics inside the data-model analyzer's report output. It holds state only and has no behaviour, so it is an application data object. It is not persisted or published as a schema, and it matters only within its module.

A pure string-escaping formatting utility used by many markdown formatters. Despite its wide use, it is a trivial helper below the granularity of an architecture element. It performs no I/O, renders no interface itself, and implements no cross-cutting concern.

Trivial state mutator on the Changeset class: it sets the status to 'committed' and bumps the modified timestamp. It has no persistence or behaviour of its own and is an implementation detail of the Changeset data object, not a standalone architectural element.

This CLI command module implements the 'info' command: it loads the model and prints the manifest and per-layer element counts. It is a named unit of application behaviour within the CLI. It renders CLI output and sets span attributes directly. Persistence is delegated to Model.load, so data_persistence is false.

A cohesive validator class composed into the main Validator. It loads bundled relationship schemas from disk and enforces catalog triples and cardinality across the model. It is a significant application component of the CLI's validation subsystem and emits telemetry spans.

A plain TypeScript interface that carries classified relationship data inside the report data model. It is an in-code data carrier with no behaviour, so it is an application DataObject. It is a minor internal type used for report generation and has no callers recorded.

A one-line convenience wrapper that delegates to findRelationshipTypes with a destination filter. It is a trivial query accessor on SpecDataLoader, an implementation detail below the granularity a maintainer would name in an architecture model.

Utility that resolves the farm workspace root via the DR_FARM_PATH env var or an upward directory walk for farm.yaml. Shared by all farm commands and the Model, so it is a notable internal function. It checks file existence on disk, which counts as persistence; it is not a standalone service.

A specific error subclass that only formats a message and suggestions for invalid JSON input, used by a single command. It is an implementation detail of CLI error handling, below the level at which an architecture model records elements.

CLI command module registering 'dr claude' subcommands (install, upgrade, remove, status, list). It is the access point through which the Claude integration manager's behaviour is reached, so it is an application interface. It drives the CLI user interface. File work is delegated to ClaudeIntegrationManager, so persistence is not flagged.

A passive TypeScript interface holding the result record for routes found in the code graph but absent from the model, used in drift analysis. It is an in-code data carrier with no behaviour, so it is an application DataObject. It is minor and has no callers.

Core logic of the CLI 'analyzer discover' command. It enumerates registered analyzer backends, detects which are installed, loads their metadata and decides selection and session-write behaviour. This is internal application behaviour called by the command handler. It does no direct persistence or UI work itself; detection and loading are delegated to callees.

This is the public entry method of the layer report generator. It assembles a markdown document from ordered sections and is called by the report orchestrator. It is internal behaviour of a reporting component, so it fits applicationfunction. It returns a string and writes no file, so no persistence concern applies.

An internal parsing and validation helper used only by NodeAIEvaluator. It extracts and validates a JSON array of node evaluations from a Claude response string. It makes no external calls itself. It is a minor internal behaviour unit of the node audit AI evaluator component.

Module defining the unified Validator that orchestrates the 5-stage model validation pipeline, composing schema, naming, reference, semantic and relationship validators. It is a central application component of the CLI. It emits tracing spans directly (startActiveSpan, setAttribute), so it carries the observability concern.

A small internal data-carrier interface holding a model name and its element ID set, used inside the composed-reference validator to cache resolved external models. It is a private implementation detail with no callers and no published schema, below the granularity a maintainer would name as an architecture element.

Core logic of the CLI add-relationship command. It resolves the source and target elements, validates the triple against the relationship catalog, checks reflexivity and duplicates, then stages the relationship or saves it via the model. This is an internal application function behind a CLI command, and it writes durable state through staging and saveRelationships.

Private helper that formats a markdown table section of a README report. It is pure string formatting, an implementation detail of ModelReadmeGenerator rather than an architecturally meaningful element. It performs no I/O and implements no cross-cutting concern.

A core class that hashes the in-memory model to create snapshots and detect drift. It is used by the staging area and changeset exporter. It is a cohesive, reusable unit with its own responsibility but plays a supporting role. It reads no storage itself, since it only hashes the in-memory model.

Module of type definitions (ComponentConfig, VersionData, FileChange, ObsoleteFile) carrying state for the integration manager, plus a light validator. These are in-code data structures passed between parts of the program, best modelled as application data objects; notable but not central. It performs no I/O itself.

Exported result type of the farm sync engine's sync operation: a passive data structure carrying status, commit range, file diffs, element mappings and changeset info between components. Not persisted or published as a schema, so it is an application DataObject of moderate significance.

Private validation step inside RelationshipValidator that checks relationship cardinality rules. It is internal behaviour of the validator component with one caller and is below the level a maintainer would name on its own. It is a minor application function and implements no cross-cutting concern.

This module implements the DataModelAnalyzer class plus its result interfaces. It analyses the architecture model's data-model layer for entities, constraints, quality issues and coverage. As a cohesive analysis unit within the tool's reporting subsystem, it is an application component. It holds an in-memory Model and does not itself persist data.

ReportGenerator is a cohesive class owned by the audit pipeline. It renders audit results into JSON, Markdown or text and writes the report files to disk. It is a notable internal component injected into PipelineOrchestrator, not a core boundary. It writes files, so data_persistence applies; it is not telemetry.

A plain TypeScript interface describing the JSON-RPC notification message shape used by the stdio client. It is a passive message payload structure, and its schema is not published, so it is an application data object. It is a minor internal type within the client file.

Inline arrow function passed as a config option to the MCP HTTP transport that returns a random UUID for session IDs. It is a trivial helper with no callers or callees, an implementation detail of transport setup rather than an architectural element.

A small query method on SpecDataService that filters relationship-catalog entries to find valid destination node types for a source. It is internal application behaviour with no callers and has low standalone architectural weight. Its reads go through the in-memory loader rather than touching durable storage directly.

A specific error subclass of CLIError carrying a fixed message and suggestions. It is error-handling boilerplate used by several commands, but it is not an architectural element. It renders no output itself and performs no persistence.

Core module centralizing all element mutations (add/update/delete) across staging and base model, handling persistence atomically and emitting telemetry logs. It is a cohesive, replaceable application unit that a maintainer would name when explaining the model's write path, so it is modelled as an application component of high significance.

Bootstraps the OpenTelemetry pipeline. It builds the Resource, the TracerProvider via NodeSDK with BatchSpanProcessor, the LoggerProvider and the exporters. This provider-level trace configuration is called from the CLI and server entry points. It also reads the manifest file from disk and wires the OTLP exporters to an external collector.

A plain exported TypeScript interface that carries entity-relationship results inside the data-model analyzer. It is an in-code data structure, neither persisted nor published as a schema, so it is an application data object. It is minor and only its module cares about it.

Utility function recursively hashing files on disk to support integration install/update comparison. It is a reusable internal helper used by BaseIntegrationManager; it reads the filesystem, but is a minor unit below service level, so it gets low significance as an application function.

Private helper method of GapAnalyzer that assigns a priority label to a relationship gap using simple string heuristics. It is an implementation detail of the analyzer with a single caller, below the granularity of an architectural element, and it implements no cross-cutting concern.

ChangesetExporter is a substantive core class that owns its storage and snapshot collaborators. It exports and imports changesets in YAML, JSON and patch formats, reads and writes files, and validates compatibility against the model. That makes it a replaceable application component used by the changeset CLI commands, and its file I/O counts as data persistence.

A CLI command module that groups the relationship subcommands (add/remove/list), validating triples against the relationship catalog and writing to the model and staging area. It is a cohesive, user-facing CLI component. It emits telemetry logs, prints CLI output and persists the model, which makes it architecturally significant within the CLI.

A small internal type describing the element fields used during PlantUML export (id, name, type, description). It has no callers listed and is an implementation detail of the exporter, below the granularity of an architectural element. It is not a meaningful data object on its own.

Core analysis routine of the model relationship audit: detects exact and semantic duplicate relationships using the catalog. It is internal behaviour invoked by the audit orchestrator, so it is an application function. It is notable within the audit module but not a service boundary. It performs no I/O and implements no cross-cutting concerns.

A trivial one-line delegating accessor on Model that forwards to GraphModel.getAllEdges. It has no callers and no logic of its own, so it is an implementation detail below architectural granularity rather than an element in its own right.

MCP tool module exposing a named 'model_reload' operation to external MCP clients; it forces a reload of the model from disk and reports a summary. It is an externally visible application capability offered via the MCP server, a notable but narrow tool among many.

A validator class that checks cross-layer references in a model. It is composed by the main Validator and is a cohesive, nameable unit of the validation subsystem. It performs no I/O and no security work, so it is an application component of moderate significance.

Trivial string-formatting helper that appends ' layer' to a formatted layer name. It is a pure utility with no architectural role. Its only callers are a validation formatter and a unit test, so it is an implementation detail rather than a model element.

Exported TypeScript interface describing a predicate catalog entry (id, predicate, inverse, category, semantics). It is a passive in-code data structure carried by the relationship catalog, not a persisted entity or published schema, so it is an application data object of moderate significance as a core domain type.

A private loading step inside the SpecDataLoader component. It reads the manifest and the per-layer JSON files from disk and sorts the layers. It is an internal behaviour unit below the level a maintainer would usually model on its own. It reads files, so data_persistence applies.

MigrationRegistry is a cohesive component that registers the spec-version migrations and applies them to architecture models. The upgrade command depends on it. It is a model-file migration engine, not database schema migrations, so it belongs in the application layer. Some migrations modify model files on disk, hence the persistence concern.

A tiny two-field internal type (severity plus message) used locally by the conformance command to collect issues. It has no callers outside its file and no behaviour. It is an implementation detail below architectural granularity, not a published schema or a meaningful data object.

A trivial helper that returns a constant list of heuristic name strings for the CBM analyzer. It holds no behaviour, I/O or contract of its own, so it is an implementation detail below architectural granularity.

Private formatting helper inside MarkdownGenerator that builds a Mermaid graph string from nodes and intra-layer edges. It is an implementation detail of the export component, below the granularity of an architecture element. It does no I/O, auth or telemetry work.

Module of TypeScript interfaces describing the in-memory structure of loaded specification metadata (layers, node types, relationships, predicates). These are pure data carriers passed between the SpecDataLoader and its consumers. They are not persisted entities or published schemas, so they map to application data objects. The module is notable but not core.

SpecDataService is a high-level facade over SpecDataLoader that exposes queries on specification layers, node types and relationships, and caches metadata. It is a central core component, held as a global singleton. File loading is delegated to the loader, so it does no persistence work itself.

A small utility module with a single helper that iterates the model's layers to find which one holds an element ID. It is a trivial lookup helper shared by commands, below the granularity of an architecture element. It does not itself perform persistence work beyond calling model accessors.

Trivial formatting helper that wraps a string in ANSI blue when colors are enabled. It has no callers and no architectural role, so it is an implementation-level utility rather than a modelled element. It only styles text and does not itself drive a user interface.

Ordered per-layer evaluation loop: for each layer it builds a prompt, invokes the Claude runner, parses the response and aggregates scores into LayerAIReview results. It is a notable internal step of the node audit orchestration. The external call is delegated to AuditAIRunner. Progress messages written to stderr count as CLI output.

A plain options bag for the CLI delete command's flags (force, cascade, dryRun, and similar). It has no behaviour and no callers in the graph. It is command-parameter boilerplate below the granularity of an architectural element. It is an attribute of the delete command at most, not a node in its own right.

Module implementing the ClaudeCodeAgent adapter, a pluggable CodingAgent that spawns the external `claude` CLI as a subprocess and parses its streaming JSON output. It is a replaceable integration component behind the CodingAgent interface, and so architecturally significant as an external integration point.

Registers the 'docs' CLI command group (generate, validate) with Commander, acting as the CLI access point through which the documentation services are reached. It is wiring only; the behaviour lives in the action handlers. It defines CLI help and options, so it drives the user interface.

A plain TypeScript interface holding audit results for one node type definition: description quality, attribute documentation ratio, issues and score. It is an in-code data carrier passed between parts of the audit module and is neither persisted nor published as a schema, so it is an application data object of minor significance.

ValidationResult is a passive in-memory carrier of validation errors and warnings, with only trivial accessors, merge and serialization. It is shared by all validators and the changeset validator, so it is a notable application data object. It is not persisted or published as a schema.

Internal behaviour of the RelationshipGraph component that builds an in-memory graph from model elements and relationships, aggregating them by spec node type for the audit orchestrator. It is a notable unit within the audit module, but it is not an exposed service. It performs no I/O, persistence or other cross-cutting work.

A passive TypeScript interface that carries aggregated model statistics into README report generation. It is an in-code data carrier and is neither persisted nor published as a schema, so it fits an application DataObject. It is a minor internal structure with no cross-cutting behaviour of its own.

MutationHandler is the unified mutation executor that both CLI commands and MCP tools use for add, update and delete. It routes each change to staging or to the base model and persists it atomically. That makes it a central application component with substantive behaviour and persistence responsibilities, not a data object.

Bundled base JSON Schema document defining the core SpecNode and SpecNodeRelationship schemas that every layer's node type extends. It is a central data-model contract for the whole specification, holding multiple $id-identified schemas, so it is best modelled as a schema document of core significance.

Trivial one-line helper that derives a cache key from an optional root path for loadModel/reloadModel. It has no behaviour of architectural interest and sits below the granularity of a modelled element.

Module housing CoverageAnalyzer, an audit component that computes relationship coverage metrics (isolation, predicate utilization, density) per layer from the relationship catalog. It is a notable internal unit of the audit subsystem rather than a core boundary. It writes partial-failure warnings to the console, which counts as CLI output; it performs no persistence.

Exported class that loads and validates .dr-verify-ignore.yaml files from disk for the verify analyzer, returning ignore rules used in drift matching. It is a cohesive, notable internal unit of the verification module, so it is modelled as an application component. It reads configuration files from disk, which counts as data persistence.

A one-line delegating accessor on SpecDataService that forwards to the loader's getStatistics. It has no logic of its own and no callers. It is a trivial wrapper below the granularity of an architecture element, and the service class itself would be the modelled element.

A plain TypeScript interface carrying metadata about a stored audit snapshot (id, timestamp, model info, path). It is an in-code data carrier passed within the snapshot storage module, not a published schema or persisted entity definition, so it is an application data object of minor significance.
