A one-line delegating accessor on Model that forwards to GraphModel.getNodesByLayer. It is a trivial wrapper with no logic of its own and no callers, so it sits below the granularity of an architecture element. The Model class itself would be the modelled component.

Enforces a read-safe permission policy for coding-agent tool permissions: an allowlist of only Bash/Read, no write access, and Bash scoped to dr CLI commands. This is authorization-constraint logic that rejects invalid configurations, closest to a policy rule. It is a notable internal unit rather than a core boundary.

Singleton managing a shared golden test model and cloning it per test: test fixture infrastructure, so it belongs in the testing layer. No listed IEEE 829 coverage type fits a fixture cache, hence the null element type. It writes the cache to a temp directory on disk, which counts as persistence. It is a notable test-support unit but not core architecture.

Module defines the Changeset domain structure (Change, StagedChange, status, Changeset class) that carries staged model modifications. It is a central concept of the spec-driven workflow, but it is primarily a state-holding data structure with trivial derived stats and no I/O, so it is modelled as an application data object.

Module defining the Importer contract plus ImportOptions/ImportResult types for format-specific importers. It is the plugin port through which import behaviour is reached, a notable internal contract rather than a data schema. It is modelled as an application interface of moderate significance and performs no cross-cutting work itself.

Public method of ConnectivityAnalyzer that computes connected components of the relationship graph for the audit feature. It is called by the audit orchestrators, making it a notable internal analysis function. It caches results only in memory, so no persistence or other cross-cutting concern applies.

A small exported interface describing one step in the mutation handler pipeline: an execute callback, a stageable flag and a description. It is an internal structural type supporting the MutationHandler component rather than a standalone architectural element. At most it would be modelled as a minor data object.

This is the MCP 'model_add' tool handler, a consumer-facing operation offered to external agents. It validates the layer, type and attributes, builds the element, and persists it to the model or stages it in a changeset via MutationHandler. It is an externally visible application service rather than an HTTP API contract.

PromptTemplates builds the LLM prompt texts used by the AI relationship-audit evaluator. It is a notable internal unit that a maintainer would name when explaining the audit AI module. It only builds strings and does not itself call external systems, persist data or render UI, so it is modelled as an application function at moderate significance.

A small CLI command options interface carrying action, id and debug flags for the audit-snapshots command. It is parameter scaffolding for a command handler, not an architectural element on its own, and performs no persistence, UI or other cross-cutting work itself.

Shared tracing helper that wraps the OTel tracer to open active spans with context propagation, record exceptions and fall back to a no-op span. It is used across CLI, model loading, validation and server code, making it the central manual-instrumentation mechanism rather than one specific span.

A cohesive validator class used by the validate command that composes the base validator with cross-model reference resolution. It loads the farm manifest and external models from disk. It is a named, replaceable component of the validation subsystem, so it is modelled as an application component of architectural significance.

Trivial re-export module wrapping a synchronous version getter in an async function for analyzer compatibility. It holds no behaviour of its own and sits below the granularity of an architectural element.

Private helper that serializes an inter-layer validation result to a JSON file in the output directory. It is an implementation detail of AIEvaluator, below the granularity of an architecture element, though it does perform file persistence.

A plain TypeScript interface carrying validation finding data (layer, message, severity, category) between validators and reporters. It is an in-code data carrier and not a published schema, so it is an application dataobject. Its significance is minor because it is a supporting type within the validator module.

A trivial counting helper used only by NodeDefinitionAnalyzer.analyze. It filters properties that have non-empty descriptions. This is an implementation detail below the granularity of an architecture element, and it has no cross-cutting concerns.

CLI command module registering the 'dr analyzer' subcommand group (discover, status, index, query, verify). It is an access point through which the analyzer services are reached by users. It renders CLI output and prompts, persists session state, and drives external analyzer backends.

Trivial accessor on ExportManager that returns registered format metadata sorted by name. It is an implementation detail of the export manager component, below modelling granularity, with no callers and no cross-cutting work.

A class that produces per-layer markdown reports (header, table of contents, statistics, Mermaid diagrams, element reference) and is constructed by ModelReportOrchestrator. It is a cohesive generator component inside the reporting module. It builds and returns strings only, with no I/O or UI rendering, so it is a notable internal component rather than a core boundary.

A plain TypeScript interface that carries the AI evaluation result for one node type within the audit module. It holds data passed between parts of the program and has no behaviour of its own. It is not persisted or published as a schema, so it is an application data object of minor significance.

A one-line formatting lambda that colours a string red with ansis for CLI output. It is a trivial presentation helper with no callers or callees and no architectural role, so it is not modelled as an element. It is too minor to count as implementing the user interface concern itself.

A trivial state-setter on the Changeset class: it sets status to 'staged' and touches the modified timestamp. This is an accessor-level implementation detail with no I/O, below the granularity of an architecture element. The enclosing Changeset class would be the element modelled instead.

Custom OpenTelemetry SpanExporter that sends spans as OTLP JSON over fetch to a collector endpoint. It defines the export destination, protocol and timeout, which is what an apm exporterconfig models. It is a telemetry integration point with an external collector.

An exported TypeScript interface in the data-model analyzer that only carries analysis result data about entity constraints. It is a passive, in-code data structure with no behaviour, not persisted or published as a schema, so it is an application data object of minor significance.

Protected path-resolution helper that locates integration source directories in dev vs production layouts. It is an internal implementation detail of BaseIntegrationManager, not a nameable architectural element. It only checks whether paths exist and does not read or write durable data.

An MCP tool handler, an entry point exposed to external agents. It validates filters, loads the model and searches elements across layers. It is an externally consumable capability (model search) offered through the MCP server, not an HTTP route. Model loading is delegated to loadModel, so data_persistence is not set; it serves an external MCP client.

Manifest is a central entity class that defines the persisted shape of the model's manifest file: project metadata, changeset history and external model declarations. It has serialization and legacy-migration logic but does no I/O itself, so it is best modelled as an object schema rather than a component. Widely used (43 callers).

A formatting module that renders verify reports as text, JSON or markdown for CLI output. It is a minor output-formatting unit inside the export subsystem. It drives user-facing CLI output, but on its own it is a low-significance application function rather than a component or service.

An in-memory registry class that indexes relationships and the relationship-type catalog by source, layer and predicate. It is a cohesive core module of the application, though it is only used by tests and is slated for consolidation into GraphModel. Moderately significant, and it implements no cross-cutting concerns.

Method of StagingAreaManager that captures a model hash for drift detection and records it on the changeset. This is internal application behaviour inside the staging component. Persistence is delegated to StagedChangesetStorage.save, so the method does not do storage work itself. It is a notable unit, but not a standalone service.

Central plugin contract for format-specific exporters: defines the access point (export method) through which export components are invoked. It is an architecturally significant extension point in the export subsystem; the interface itself performs no persistence or I/O.

Factory that constructs the MCP server, registers its tool and resource surfaces, and warms the model cache. It is the assembly point for the MCP integration boundary that external agents connect to, so it is best modelled as the MCP server application component. It does not itself persist data; the model loading is delegated to loadModel.

A small utility module of string-formatting helpers that title-case node type names and produce markdownlint-safe link text. It is a pure formatting utility with no callers listed and no architectural role, so it falls below the granularity of a model element.
